custom-water-bottle.title: Custom Plastic Water Bottles for Wholesale & Private Label
custom-water-bottle.lead: Build a coherent bottle range from an approved model, material, closure and branding specification — not from a catalog photo alone.
custom-water-bottle.overview: Most projects can start with an established XUYI plastic bottle model, then refine the capacity, body and lid colors, decoration and retail presentation. A new bottle silhouette or unusual drinking mechanism takes a different engineering and tooling route. We help B2B buyers define that route before a final quotation or production commitment.

sections.heading: Start with the right bottle architecture
sections.body: Sports bottles, children's straw bottles, shaker cups and large water jugs have different lids, carrying loads and cleaning requirements. Choose a product family and exact model first; identify whether the project changes decoration only or the component geometry. A 600 mL bottle body cannot automatically accept a larger closure or straw simply because the threads look similar.
checks: Identify the product SKU and preferred volume
Confirm cap type, straw, seal and carry handle
Decide what can remain a standard stock component

sections.heading: Material decisions: PC, Tritan, PP and PETG
sections.body: Body, lid, straw and gasket do not always share one polymer. Clarify intended water temperature, permitted cleaning conditions, transparency, finish and destination market. Conventional BPA-based PC should not be marketed as BPA-free without product-specific evidence. Resin grade, colorants and the final assembled product must be reviewed for any food-contact or BPA-free statement.
checks: State whether BPA-free is a contractual requirement
Specify intended liquid, temperature and cleaning
Ask for component-level material and supporting evidence

sections.heading: Custom appearance without redesigning the bottle
sections.body: Many private-label projects use existing molded bodies with a selected solid color, compatible logo print and buyer-designed packaging. Gradients, translucent colors, multi-position graphics or different lid colors are possible only where compatible with the selected resin and manufacturing route. Custom color minimums may apply independently to lids and bodies.
checks: Provide a color reference or Pantone target
Ask which decoration area is actually printable
Confirm color minimums and logo setup fees

sections.heading: Validate the sample as a complete retail SKU
sections.body: Approve the actual bottle plus lid, straw or mixer insert, packing components and graphics together. Review assembled appearance, seal placement, repeated opening, surface scuffs, print placement and the information required for your sales market. Images alone are not acceptance samples. Record the approved artwork version and component specification for repeat production.
checks: Approve the precise body and lid combination
Keep a decorated reference sample
Specify packaging and product labeling

sections.heading: Create a comparable wholesale RFQ
sections.body: Include quantity by color, model numbers, logo positions, packaging choices, target delivery date and destination. Ask the factory to separate unit costs, decoration/tooling setup, sample cost, test requests and packing requirements. MOQ and lead time must be quoted for the final variant, not inferred from a general 'custom water bottle' claim.
checks: Request quote by SKU and quantity tier
Define destination and shipping term
Document any material or design exclusions

faqs.question: Can we customize an existing bottle without a new mold?
faqs.answer: Often, provided the requested colors, logo and pack work with the selected stock design. A new bottle structure, embossed graphic or closure may require tooling.

faqs.question: Which plastic is best for BPA-free bottles?
faqs.answer: No material name alone proves a whole assembled bottle is BPA-free. Tritan, PP and PETG are options to assess; request product-specific statements and applicable test evidence.

faqs.question: Will the sample match the mass-production order?
faqs.answer: The sample should be approved against a controlled bill of materials, decoration file and pack specification. Changes require review before production.

faqs.question: How do we get an accurate wholesale price?
faqs.answer: Send the chosen model, variant details, quantity tiers, artwork, destination and packing requirement. Pricing and MOQ depend on these details.

custom-molding.title: Custom Plastic Bottle Molding & Tooling Development
custom-molding.lead: Understand when an injection-molded cap, a new bottle body, or a revised drinking system needs dedicated tooling and validation.
custom-molding.overview: A truly custom bottle is an engineering project, not a print job. The body-forming process, cap and handle construction, polymer behavior and tolerances affect the mold route. We can discuss feasibility through the suitable XUYI or manufacturing-partner production route; engineering capability, tooling costs and ownership are confirmed per project.

sections.heading: Define precisely what changes require tooling
sections.body: A printed logo and standard body color usually do not require a new cavity. New body geometry, an integrated handle, neck thread or cap shape may. Mark whether the requested change affects appearance only or water sealing and mechanical function. The second class needs more careful fit, assembly and durability evaluation.
checks: Draw body and neck dimensions
List revised lid, cap, straw and gasket parts
Separate cosmetic changes from functional changes

sections.heading: Select appropriate body and component forming methods
sections.body: Injection molding is commonly associated with caps, small handles and complex plastic components; plastic bottle bodies may use blow-molding or other processes depending on polymer, design and manufacturing route. The mold maker must verify resin suitability, wall thickness, draft, shrinkage and neck tolerances. Do not describe all bottles as injection-molded products.
checks: Confirm resin and finished wall/weight targets
Review whether the body uses blowing or another suitable process
Ask for neck, cap and seal fit checks

sections.heading: Design-for-manufacture before cutting steel
sections.body: Before committing to a mold, assess the 2D/3D part definition, parting line, surface finish, draft angles, undercuts, gate and ejector positions if relevant, and assembly interfaces. Evaluate where sinks, flash or deformation would be unacceptable. Review how changing the bottle capacity could affect mold size, carton dimensions and lid alignment.
checks: Review engineering drawings and samples
Document critical sealing and thread tolerances
Agree visible surface and finish expectations

sections.heading: Prototypes, trial shots and acceptance
sections.body: A visual 3D model cannot validate liquid containment or assembly quality. Where feasible, use prototypes to check handling and mechanical layout, then inspect molded trial samples for fit, appearance, dimensional stability, closure function and relevant material evidence. Decide defect acceptance, rework and pilot approval before production quantities are committed.
checks: Review first samples with the actual cap/gasket
Record leakage or opening-force test conditions
Approve signed drawings and reference sample

sections.heading: Commercial responsibilities and mold ownership
sections.body: A responsible quote separates design services, tooling charges, sample trials and ongoing per-unit costs. Clarify in writing ownership and storage of molds, maintenance responsibility, design-file access, revision allowances and transfer rights, when applicable. NDA, exclusivity and third-party supplier involvement should be agreed rather than implied.
checks: Ask who owns and stores each tool

faqs.question: Do custom bottles always need injection molding?
faqs.answer: No. Caps and certain parts are commonly injection molded, while bottle bodies may use suitable blow-forming or other processes. The engineering route depends on resin and geometry.

faqs.question: Does a new printed logo require a new mold?
faqs.answer: Normally not for compatible surface printing. An integrated embossed or debossed logo may require tooling changes.

faqs.question: Who owns the mold?
faqs.answer: Ownership and use rights must be specified in the tooling contract and cannot be assumed from a one-time fee.

faqs.question: Can you quote a mold from a photograph?
faqs.answer: A photograph supports initial screening, but accurate quotes require dimensions, part geometry, material and production targets.

custom-logo.title: Custom Logo Printing & Private Label Bottle Branding
custom-logo.lead: Choose an appropriate way to put a brand on a curved plastic bottle — with confirmed print area, color and abrasion performance.
custom-logo.overview: A logo that looks perfect on a flat PDF can distort on a tapered sports bottle or lose contrast on a translucent wall. We work from the actual bottle surface, resin grade, desired artwork and quantity to review suitable print or decoration options. Screen, pad, compatible transfers or other methods are considered case by case rather than promised for every polymer.

sections.heading: Map the real logo area first
sections.body: Request a printing-layout drawing or a photograph annotated with maximum width, height and distance from handles, ribs or seams. Fix the orientation of the logo relative to the spout and lid. A curved surface changes perceived proportions and may constrain multi-color registration. Separate bottle-body artwork from cap and retail-box artwork.
checks: Provide a vector logo in AI, EPS or PDF
Specify the viewing position relative to the lid
Confirm minimum line widths and safe margins

sections.heading: Compare the process instead of chasing buzzwords
sections.body: Screen printing is useful for some single or limited-color designs; pad printing can address smaller or irregular areas where technically feasible. Transfer or digital processes may enable more complex artwork but demand compatible plastic, inks and curing. Laser processes developed for stainless tumblers are not automatically suitable for PP, Tritan, PC or PETG.
checks: Confirm ink compatibility with the exact resin
Ask about color count and registration
Request a physical printed sample

sections.heading: Color management, white underprint and transparency
sections.body: Brand colors appear different against opaque black, translucent pastel and transparent bodies. White ink backing or adjusted color separation may be necessary. Define Pantone or other references with a tolerance agreement, and evaluate the print on the actual molded-color sample under normal light rather than relying on monitor mockups.
checks: Provide artwork and preferred color values
Test contrast on every important body color
Approve a realistic decorated physical sample

sections.heading: Print durability and food-contact boundaries
sections.body: Normal handling, cleaning and rubbing can damage some decorations. Agree on an appropriate adhesion, rub and cleaning test and inspect the printed sample after testing. Confirm where printing sits relative to drinking-contact areas and retailer packaging claims. Do not advertise permanent, scratchproof or dishwasher-safe printing without evidence tied to the chosen process.
checks: Keep decoration away from undesired contact areas
Agree test method and pass criteria
Control ink/process changes on repeat orders

sections.heading: Make the purchase order precise
sections.body: Quote and approve logo size, print locations, ink colors, setup charges, unit print cost and packaging artwork as separate fields. Complex graphics and each SKU/color variation can change the minimum order. Keep revision IDs and a physical golden sample so a reorder does not drift from the original approved mark.
checks: Record artwork revision and position
Ask MOQ per design/color combination
Approve packaging copy separately

faqs.question: Can I print full-color artwork on any plastic bottle?
faqs.answer: Not universally. Feasibility depends on curved geometry, plastic resin, surface treatment, production method and run size.

faqs.question: Should my logo be supplied as a PNG?
faqs.answer: PNG can show the intended visual result, but editable vector artwork generally provides more reliable production dimensions and separations.

faqs.question: Can the same printed artwork fit different bottle sizes?
faqs.answer: Usually the design must be mapped separately to each printable area; size and curvature changes may require a new proof.

faqs.question: Is laser engraving standard for plastic bottles?
faqs.answer: No. It is not a universal plastic decoration method and must be reviewed for the exact resin and part. Do not assume metal-bottle techniques transfer directly.

custom-graphics.title: Custom Bottle Colors, Patterns & Graphic Finishes
custom-graphics.lead: Plan solid colors, transparent and translucent styles, gradients and printed patterns without confusing mockup possibilities with mass-production feasibility.
custom-graphics.overview: Color and surface design often determine whether a bottle looks like a recognizable retail collection. But a Pantone value, a molded pigment and a decorated gradient are different production choices. They need different materials, process checks, minimum order quantities and physical sampling; XUYI reviews them against the selected bottle shape and actual plastic substrate.

sections.heading: Plan molded color separately from artwork
sections.body: When the bottle body color is made through resin coloring, the result is affected by material, wall thickness, transparency and mold texture. A visual gradient may instead depend on a specific compatible decoration method. A rendered design does not prove a particular model can be mass-produced with that effect. Agree on what is solid molded color and what is later printing.
checks: Choose opaque, translucent or transparent
Specify body and lid colors separately
Clarify whether artwork is in-mold or applied afterward

sections.heading: Build a workable color palette
sections.body: Provide Pantone targets or a physical color chip, while recognizing that digital RGB images rarely match molded resin exactly. Test colors under normal lighting on the actual bottle. Transparent bodies can alter the appearance of white, pastel and dark printed graphics. Specify which deviations are acceptable in volume production.
checks: Select primary and alternate approved samples
Review print visibility on translucent bodies
Approve acceptable color variation

sections.heading: Understand solid, gradient and wraparound treatments
sections.body: A solid pigment often depends on molding material and lot size; a gradient or wraparound pattern may require a verified transfer, screen/digital system or different finishing process. Complex continuous graphics can break around handles, ribs and tapered shapes. Request a production feasibility check with the bottle maker, particularly for PP and other difficult-to-print surfaces.
checks: Map design across ribs and seams
Confirm method compatible with selected resin
Review minimum graphic details and registration

sections.heading: Surface texture changes appearance and handling
sections.body: Matte and glossy tools create different look and tactile feel. Soft-feel coating or overmolded grip is a different component/process decision and cannot be promised just because an image depicts a textured bottle. Check scuff marks, fingerprint visibility, rub performance and cleaning conditions on approved samples.
checks: Specify molded texture vs applied coating
Review grip zones and logo overlap
Check cleaning/rub behavior

sections.heading: Synchronize design with MOQ and repeat orders
sections.body: A combination of body color, contrasting cap color, gradient design and full-color packaging may have multiple production minimums. Build a SKU matrix showing body, lid, graphic version and carton variation. Agree on a signed appearance reference and confirm how many colorways can be packed together for the delivery channel.

Separate mold-color and decoration setup fees
Keep final appearance reference for reorders

faqs.question: Can a photo's gradient be matched exactly?
faqs.answer: A photo is a starting point. Final visual results depend on substrate, ink/process, lighting and approval tolerances. A decorated sample is required.

faqs.question: Can I order one different cap color for every bottle?
faqs.answer: It depends on stock availability and minimum quantities for each separately molded component. Confirm the requested color matrix.

faqs.question: Does translucent mean the same thing as Tritan?
faqs.answer: No. Translucency describes appearance; Tritan is a resin family. Multiple plastics can have different optical properties.

faqs.question: How should we approve color accuracy?
faqs.answer: Use agreed color references plus actual samples under controlled viewing conditions; keep a signed sample for future orders.

custom-manufacturing.title: Plastic Drinkware Manufacturing & Quality Coordination
custom-manufacturing.lead: Connect an approved design to materials, forming, closure assembly, decoration, inspection and packed shipment through a controlled specification.
custom-manufacturing.overview: Production quality is determined by the approved bottle specification, reliable component sourcing and checks at appropriate stages. XUYI coordinates its own and relevant manufacturing-partner processes depending on the model. We do not claim that every part or technique is produced on one particular machine or that a fixed capacity applies to all designs.

sections.heading: Translate the approved sample into a production specification
sections.body: A purchase order should be traceable to a model/variant, component bill of materials, signed sample, artwork revision and pack instruction. For bottle bodies and closures, the specification may include wall dimensions, neck/thread fit, material grade and color. Without a controlled reference, two batches can look similar but have different sealing or label behavior.
checks: Record body, lid, seal and accessory versions
Approve a reference sample and printable file
Document parts that require buyer approval before substitution

sections.heading: Understand forming, assembly and surface-decoration steps
sections.body: Caps, handles and selected small parts may be injection molded; bottle bodies can use other forming processes based on shape and polymer. Components are then assembled with gaskets, straws or inserts as specified. Printing, transfer or other surface work is checked on the actual substrate. Each process needs suitable controls rather than a universal 'fully automated' promise.
checks: Match tooling method to exact component
Check molding flash, threads and clarity
Inspect printed and assembled details separately

sections.heading: Material identification and incoming quality
sections.body: Confirm resin grade and component material declarations for body, lid, seals, straw and any colorants. Buyers needing BPA-free or food-contact documentation should state the destination rules and intended use at the start. A report for another brand or product model cannot automatically be treated as this specific bottle's evidence.
checks: Review component-level material list
Ask for evidence for destination markets
Control resin and color changes

sections.heading: In-process and final inspection
sections.body: Depending on the product, checks may cover visual marks, capacity, dimensions, print position, lid operation, missing seals, assembly cleanliness and selected leak or impact tests. A written sample plan should define the method and acceptance criteria. '100% leakproof' or 'zero defects' should not be used without clear support.
checks: Define critical, major and minor defects
Check assembly and close/open consistency
Document failures and corrective steps

sections.heading: Bulk packing, traceability and shipping release
sections.body: Review the retail pack and master carton against the approved specification. Check carton counts, size and weight, label information, product color assortments and export handover requirements. The factory and any partner suppliers should know how to identify affected lots when a component or artwork change occurs.
checks: Inspect cartons and labels
Retain shipment and batch references
Confirm delivery terms and loading instructions

faqs.answer: Manufacturing location and processes can differ by model. Confirm the specific production route and any approved partner involvement during quotation.

custom-packaging.title: Custom Water Bottle Packaging & Export Carton Design
custom-packaging.lead: Choose retail presentation and master cartons that protect decorated bottles, communicate your brand and fit import requirements.
custom-packaging.overview: A wholesale bottle becomes a sellable SKU only when the physical product, accessories, labels and packing agree. Retail color boxes, sleeves, protective bags and bulk cartons have different costs and freight footprints. We develop packing requirements from the selected plastic bottle and destination market rather than assuming one generic box works for every cap or handle.

sections.heading: Choose retail-ready or bulk-first pack formats
sections.body: Simple individual bags or sleeves may be practical for promotional orders, while branded folding cartons and gift packs support retail shelves. Bottle shape, cap height, handles, mixer inserts and straps can change the interior footprint. Decide whether the consumer expects a single bottle, bundled accessories or a multipack, then specify the contents precisely.
checks: Confirm bottle and accessories per sales unit
Identify retail versus wholesale distribution
Choose simple protection or branded presentation

sections.heading: Design the protective structure around a real sample
sections.body: Transparent plastic surfaces and printed logos can scuff during transit if items touch. Paper wrap, inserts, dividers or compartment arrangements may be considered, subject to cost and packaging sustainability targets. Approve how the lid is secured and any loose accessories are retained. Do not use stock packaging pictures as proof of the proposed shipping strength.
checks: Measure packed bottle including lid/handle
Decide insert, divider or sleeve needs
Inspect packaging abrasion on samples

sections.heading: Finish carton engineering with measured data
sections.body: Request units per carton, carton external dimensions, gross/net weight and handling or pallet information where applicable. Large jugs and compact sports bottles have very different freight volume per unit. Compare shipping terms and landed cost using real carton configurations. Carton compression or transit test methods are chosen for the actual route and retailer needs.
checks: Approve units/carton and outer dimensions
Confirm gross weight and carton marking
Validate stacking and transport conditions

sections.heading: Prepare artwork and legally appropriate labels
sections.body: Print-ready artwork should identify dielines, bleed/safe areas, barcodes, warnings, capacity, market language and any importer details required by the buyer's destination. Do not carry over group-site claims such as universal FDA/LFGB certification, 'eco' or BPA-free without model-specific evidence. The buyer should approve legal copy and symbol usage before packaging prints.
checks: Provide vector art and barcode data
Confirm language, warnings and destination rules
Sign off carton design and revision

sections.heading: Control order assembly and shipping records
sections.body: For mixed-color cartons, decide which SKU/color and how many go in every case. Agree whether product labels and cartons identify body and cap variants, whether serial/lot traceability is needed and who supplies shipping documents. Packing photos, carton counts and a final specification reduce disputes and customer returns.
checks: Confirm SKU and color breakdown per carton
Check printed carton marks and pack list
Retain version control for reorders

faqs.answer: Yes when packaging is feasible for the selected product. Minimum quantities and carton costs vary with print colors and dieline.

faqs.question: Can we mix bottle colors in a single master carton?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but the packing list, labels and production quantities need to specify the distribution clearly.

faqs.question: Who supplies barcode and destination warnings?
faqs.answer: The buyer or its appointed regulatory representative should approve required local wording, barcode data and compliance claims.

faqs.question: Can packing reduce freight cost?
faqs.answer: Improved carton utilization can help, but actual savings depend on carton dimensions, weight, transport mode and handling constraints.
